sections.overview: The oscar is a large South American freshwater cichlid native to the Amazon and Orinoco drainages, widely kept in aquariums and also eaten locally.
sections.identification: Its deep oval body, large mouth and dark ground colour with orange-red markings are distinctive; adults commonly reach about 24 centimetres and can exceed 40.
sections.habitat: Oscars inhabit warm, quiet, shallow freshwater habitats such as sluggish channels, ponds and floodplain waters with muddy or sandy bottoms.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly near the bottom, taking snails, shrimp, insects and other small animals, while field accounts also report small fish and crayfish.
sections.behavior: Pairs clean and defend spawning surfaces, and both parents guard eggs and young; the species is a popular aquarium fish but grows relatively slowly.
sections.reproduction: This open-substrate spawner lays adhesive eggs on a cleaned flat surface; both parents tend the clutch, and eggs typically hatch within three or four days.
sections.ecology: As a generalist predator and benthic feeder, it links small invertebrates and fish to larger predators; introduced populations can persist outside its native range.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment classifies the oscar as Least Concern, although local assessments can differ and non-native populations are documented in several regions.
